courses.description: High School Structured Writing is a systematic approach to applying metacognitive and executive functioning strategies to the writing process. Specifically, students will: learn to read complex texts for understanding and comprehension; apply metacognitive strategies to the five phases of academic writing - brainstorming, organizing, drafting, revising, and publishing; and develop their academic vocabulary and grammar structures while reading and writing. Writing instruction progresses from basic to expanded sentences through thesis statements and 5 paragraph essays. Comprehension and metacognitive strategies include text annotation, two-column notes, summarizing, self-questioning, and structured discussions. The course is organized around a yearly theme and includes opportunities for students to apply their writing skills to areas of personal and community interest. This is an elective.
courses.prerequisites: Recommendation of the IEP Team or approval from the Learning Opportunities Coordinator

courses.description: Eating is an agricultural act and one we participate in every day in order to sustain ourselves. In Regenerative Agriculture, students will work in a hands-on capacity both indoors and out to gain knowledge about how to grow their own food by using regenerative practices such as assessing and building soil health, no-till, cover cropping, organic pest management and biodiversity. Students will learn about starting plants from seed and transplanting practices from our greenhouse to our garden. Students will be planting, harvesting, preparing and eating food grown in our school garden. Students will be responsible for growing, harvesting, and processing microgreens for our staff CSA. Students will be involved with maple sugaring production at the King Farm. Students will get to learn about and visit local farms using these practices as well as plan their own biologically diverse garden model.
courses.notes: Listed as "REGENERATIVE AGRICULTURE *Spring (previously named Foundations of Agriculture)". Foundational Course CRAFT Credential: Take prior to Sustainable Food Systems. Also described in the CRAFT section (p.52, same text). This course counts towards the CRAFT credential.

courses.description: The way our food is grown, processed, transported and distributed is part of a complex system that depends on social, economic and environmental factors. In this course, students will apply a systems thinking lens to understand their place in the food system and find leverage points for making sustainable changes. Students will participate in native plant production, seed saving, and composting as part of a thriving local food system model. Students will be responsible for growing, harvesting and distributing our staff microgreen CSA. Students will get to harvest, prepare and eat locally grown food while tracing the path various foods take to get to their plate. Students will visit local producers to see the process of making various VT products.

courses.description: Woodstock Union High School offers the opportunity to take online courses through two online-learning providers: VHS Learning and Vermont Virtual Learning Cooperative (VTVLC). Through these partnerships, students have access to over 200 full-year and semester online courses including Advanced Placement (AP), Honors-level, and Standard-level courses. Online courses can be used to explore subjects not taught in person at the high school or to resolve scheduling conflicts for in-person classes. To be successful in online learning, students need to possess strong independent work skills and be motivated to engage with the curriculum material. It is expected that students will participate in their online course on a regular basis and complete assignments in a timely way.

courses.description: Vermont’s Dual Enrollment program allows high school juniors and seniors to take two free courses at participating Vermont colleges and universities. Students may take the courses anytime during the summer before their junior year through the spring of their senior year. The Vermont State Dual Enrollment Program is a college-level course that becomes part of the student’s transcript. This credit counts towards sports eligibility and full-time student status. These courses are not weighted and not part of the student’s GPA. Through the Dual Enrollment program, students are eligible to take courses through the following Vermont colleges/ universities. Vermont State University (VTSU), Community College of Vermont (CCV), University of Vermont (UVM). Given Woodstock’s distance from these campuses, almost all dual-enrollment courses will be online. The school offers another kind of dual enrollment called “concurrent enrollment,” where a college course is taught on our campus by one of our faculty. Currently we offer College Stats and College Algebra.
